result.edits:
I approve all five cards. I made edits to /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/research/coldstart_C04/hypotheses_r1.yaml. They change only how variants are written and read, not the hypotheses themselves. The count is unchanged at 64 variants (H1 17 / H2 12 / H3 16 / H4 11 / H5 8). After the edits, c04_check returns ADMISSIBLE (exit 0), and every expression parses under the strict grammar (allow_general=False). A "总领审定" block in the file header records all of the following.

0. The most important finding: E1 Q6(iii)'s claim that "1e-6 noise lifts the dispersion score to 1.00" does not hold on the real operators.
   - Dispersion is computed in partura/diagnose.py distinct_fraction as the median over days of (distinct values / names).
   - The Log* fields are stored by taking the log in float64 and casting to float32, and the operators run in float32. For stocks with no event, P, FR, NS and their differences are not continuous noise. They are ties sitting on 1 to 5 float32 grid points.
   - I simulated 3000 stocks with no events, using the registry operators and E1's storage method:
     - cross_delta(P,15) and cross_delta(P,3): 0.002
     - ΔFR(60): 0.001
     - U60×(−R60): 0.10
     - FR minus its one-year mean: 0.10
     - With back-adjusted prices rounded to 0.01, cross_delta(P,15) is still only 0.08.
   - PAY passes the gate only because roughly 60–70% of stocks paid out in the past year.
   - Consequence: under the original design, H2 was left with only v3/v10 (a single construction), and H3 with only v2. Rule (a), which needs two different constructions, could never be met.
   - Fixes:
     - H2/v4 is now a second based construction (30-day linear decay + PAY), role core.
     - H2/v5, v6, v7 are rewritten to share v3's base and differ from it in one place only.
     - H3/v6, v7, v8, v10, v13 are rewritten as pairs with v2: same 0.04 base, one difference each.
     - H3/v14 gets a base and is promoted to core.
     - The unbased mechanism variants are kept, and each one's predicts now states its gate expectation. A gate failure of H2/v12 directly shows that the identity holds at float32 precision.
1. Three variants were certain gate failures:
   - H5/v5: equal-weight sign mean gives 0.02 → changed to cross_decay_linear, which gives 0.75.
   - H5/v8 (share of days with a price change): 0.006 equal-weight, 0.24 linear-weight → replaced with volatility-adjusted momentum, PRET/(std+0.002).
   - H3/v8: multiplying by 0 for stocks already listed on the view's first day → given a base.
2. H4:
   - The text "price only jumps on ex-rights days, turnover < 0.02" contradicted C03 B2, where log(Close) had 0.055 turnover after residualization. Changed to 0.03–0.06.
   - fails_if (e) "v4/v5 ≥ v1 means reject" would fire almost every time once size is neutralized, because log price = log cap − log shares. It now triggers only when v4/v5 are well above v1.
   - Added (f): the card has only one construction, so a pass can only be recorded as "the signal exists".
   - novelty now names C03's 602A family (long the highest back-adjusted prices, same direction as this card).
   - v4/v5 now carry a 40% risk of being rejected by the known-family correlation.
   - v6 now has a caveat about Volume units differing by board.
3. H1:
   - mechanism now states that the long leg is in practice high dividend yield and cannot be separated from value, industry or SOE style.
   - fails_if (b) now uses v17 as the deciding reading; v11 scoring high on its own no longer rejects.
   - v5, v8 and v10 now carry gate expectations.
4. H2/v12: removed "dividends are almost impossible within 3 days" and added the share-count / adjustment-factor date-mismatch reading for the stock-split season.
5. H1/v4 and H4/v3: noted that ChiNext was also 10% before 2020-08-24.

I checked the code but changed nothing for this: long_neutral does not use the untradable mask, so the ListAge gates on H1/v9 and H4/v7 do have an effect.

The simulation scripts are /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-wxy-Desktop-AlphaCube/84cd2fa5-62ee-4d6f-b035-b604567ee88d/scratchpad/c04w1_zl/quant_sim.py, /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-wxy-Desktop-AlphaCube/84cd2fa5-62ee-4d6f-b035-b604567ee88d/scratchpad/c04w1_zl/quant_sim_round.py and /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-wxy-Desktop-AlphaCube/84cd2fa5-62ee-4d6f-b035-b604567ee88d/scratchpad/c04w1_zl/quant_sim2.py. I did not change code or the PLAN, did not run servers or GPU, and did not commit.
result.predictions:
Written before any results. "Pass" means any variant with score ≥ 0.5 that is not rejected by correlation. P(all 64 variants < 0.5) ≈ 50%. The median number of hypotheses with a passing variant is 0–1. The most likely single reading is H1 at +1, then the reversal component in H3.

Gate:
- H2/v12 fails the dispersion gate: 60%.
- H2/v1 and v2 fail: 70%.
- H3/v1, v3 and v5 fail: 75%.
- H3/v4 passes the gate on grid jitter.
- H1/v1 passes the gate: 85%.
- The rewritten H5/v5 and v8 pass: 90%.

H1 (net payout):
- Some core passes: 25%. Conditional on passing, direction +1 (long high payout): 85%.
- Train is the binding leg (train < valid): 85%. Turnover 0.025–0.045.
- |v11 − v12| < 0.2: 70%.

H2 (ex-dividend clientele):
- Some core passes: 15%. Almost only through the based v3 / v4 / v10, i.e. H1 plus a dividend-season boost, so it rises and falls with H2/v8 (= H1/v1).
- v3 − v8 > 0.1 (H2 adds something over H1): 35%. Direction +1.

H3 (unlock then reversal):
- Some variant passes: 18%. Direction +1, long the stocks that have already fallen.
- The variants most likely to pass are the based v2 / v14 / v16 and the 60-day reversal control v11. "Passes but the mechanism fails (fails_if (b))" is more likely than "mechanism holds", about 2 : 1.

H4 (nominal price):
- Some core passes: 10%. Direction uncertain, +1 : −1 ≈ 55 : 45. Train and valid favoured opposite styles (large-cap high-price in 2019–2020, micro-cap low-price in 2022–2023), so the min of the two is hard to clear either way.
- |v6 − v1| < 0.1: 75%.
- At least one of v4 / v5 rejected by known-family correlation: 40%.

H5 (frog in the pan):
- Some core passes: 12%. If it passes, −1 (long one-year losers, which also benefits from survivorship bias) vs +1 is 55 : 45. A pass in the opposite direction is rejected under rule (c).
